oil.summary: Crude ended Friday modestly lower on the day — WTI -0.99% to $71.35, Brent -0.63% to $75.82 — but both contracts locked in strong weekly gains of roughly 4-6% driven by a sharp re-escalation in Middle East risk. The U.S. revoked Iran's sanctions waiver following tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and reports of U.S. strikes on 80 Iranian targets kept the risk premium elevated. Ukraine's drone campaign against Russian oil depots in Stavropol and Tver, as well as strikes targeting 12 tankers, prompted Moscow to ban diesel exports, tightening distillate supply globally and pushing refining margins to reported record highs. RBOB gasoline was the stark outlier, cratering 8.02% on the session. Partially offsetting supply concerns, the UAE posted record output of 4.1 million bpd in June, and India's ONGC announced a 12.8-million-barrel strategic reserve build.
drivers: U.S. revocation of Iran sanctions waiver and Hormuz tensions sustain weekly crude risk premium
Russia's diesel export ban and Ukrainian strikes on depots/tankers drive distillate tightness and record refining margins
UAE record output of 4.1 mb/d and ONGC strategic reserve build provide partial demand/supply offsets

gas.summary: Natural gas markets delivered a split session on July 10. Henry Hub slid 3.98% to $2.891/MMBtu, extending a steep weekly loss of 9.51%, suggesting domestic U.S. fundamentals remain bearish despite the broader geopolitical backdrop. European TTF also softened on the day, down 3.37% to €48.415/MWh, though it retained a strong 10% weekly gain, reflecting greater European sensitivity to Hormuz and Russian supply disruptions. LNG flow data offered a nuanced signal: close to half a dozen LNG carriers transited the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, suggesting trade has not fully halted despite hostilities. ADNOC's $900 million order for four newbuild LNG carriers signals longer-term Abu Dhabi export ambition. A UK High Court ruling denied Nord Stream AG's $662 million insurance claim, applying a war exclusion clause.
drivers: Henry Hub in sharp weekly retreat (-9.51%), pointing to loose U.S. domestic balances despite geopolitical noise
TTF retains large weekly gain (+10%) on European exposure to Hormuz LNG transit risk and Russian supply disruption
LNG carriers continuing Hormuz transits and ADNOC's $900M newbuild order underline long-term Gulf export expansion intent

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 0.84% on the day to $75.35/EUA, holding a month-to-date gain of 3.16% even as TTF softened, a modest divergence worth watching. Headline flow for the power and carbon complex was thin on direct price catalysts today. Thematically, NTPC — India's largest utility — disclosed it is actively seeking to acquire global uranium assets to underpin a planned nuclear expansion, signalling long-term emerging-market baseload investment. A commentary piece flagged permitting bureaucracy as a structural bottleneck strangling U.S. clean energy development, while a separate piece framed power — particularly for AI data centres — as the defining resource competition of the current era. The broader geopolitical polycrisis, including Hormuz tensions and the Russia-Ukraine infrastructure war, was cited as compounding pressure on already strained power and carbon markets.
drivers: EUAs inch higher (+0.84%) despite softer TTF, maintaining a positive month-to-date trend
NTPC pursuing global uranium acquisitions to fuel India's planned nuclear buildout, a structural long-term demand signal
U.S. clean energy permitting bottlenecks and AI-driven power demand growth identified as key medium-term structural themes
